archetype.name: Playoff Team (extra-possession)
archetype.definition: A team that wins the possession battle rather than the shooting battle: it crashes the offensive glass, forces turnovers and protects the ball well enough to outscore teams it can't outshoot, with a defense that bleeds at the rim.

report.headline: Toronto wins on extra possessions; the jumper and the rim defense decide its ceiling
report.take:
Toronto at 5-4 is a better team than that record looks, but not by much, and it gets there in an unusual way. The offense ranks 9th by ORtg (117) even though it is near the bottom of the league in both 3P % (31.5, 27th) and 3PA Rate (37.6, 27th). The difference is volume. The Raptors lead the league in ORB % (32.7) and in Opp TOV % (17.7), sit 5th in TOV % (12.1) and 8th in FT Rate. They take more shots than their opponents, get to the line, and rarely give the ball away. That profile is new. Last season's 46-36 team had an ORB % of 25.5 and an Opp TOV % of 14.3, and it won with a 5th-ranked defense and better shooting.

The defense is 11th by DRtg (111.6), and the turnovers do much of the work. When opponents do get a shot up, it is a good one: Opp Rim FG % is 71 (28th) against a league average of 65.2, Opp Rim Rate is 26th, and Opp eFG % is 54.8 (21st). By position, shooting guards have had their way, scoring 36.33 points a game against Toronto, the most in the league. Power forwards, by contrast, have been held to 13, 2nd fewest. The perimeter attack is getting through, and the rim isn't stopping it.

The margin is flattered by a few blowouts. Wins of 135-92 over Chicago and 129-99 over Orlando did heavy lifting in a 3-2 October in which Toronto allowed 106.2 a game. November has been 2-2, with 121 allowed a game. Over the last five, the defense gave up 8.22 more points a game than its season mark and the differential turned to -2.2. That stretch came mostly on a road trip through LAL, LAC, DEN and MIL, so some of it is schedule. The W vs Pt Diff of -1 says the record, if anything, slightly trails the margin.

The roster adds uncertainty. Kawhi Leonard, 6th on the small-forward tab, has played two games and is listed Out. Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley, the two highest-usage healthy pieces, are both Day-To-Day. The direction from here hinges on whether the shooting climbs back toward last year's 35.4 and whether the turnover-forcing holds. Both are plausible: the first should, the second probably fades some.

strengths.title: Winning the possession count
strengths.body: Toronto leads the league in both ORB % and Opp TOV %, and its own TOV % is 5th-lowest. That combination manufactures shots that a below-average shooting team needs to stay 9th by ORtg. The offensive rebounding is a jump from last season's 25.5 and probably partly reflects who is on the floor. The opponent turnover rate is the more likely of the two to drift back toward the league's 13.8.

strengths.title: Scoring efficiency despite cold shooting
strengths.body: An ORtg of 117 sits 3.6 points above the league despite a 3P % 3.2 points below it. That makes the offense look resilient rather than lucky: the shooting is the part most likely to improve. FT Rate (8th) adds a steady source of points that doesn't depend on jumpers falling.

strengths.title: Lockdown on power forwards
strengths.body: Opposing power forwards have scored 13 a game and take a much smaller share of the points against Toronto than they do league-wide. With Barnes and Murray-Boyles both listed at the position, this looks structural rather than random. Even so, nine games is a small sample for position splits.

concerns.title: No resistance at the rim
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 71 at the rim, 5.8 points above the league, and they get there more often than against most teams. Last season the Opp Rim FG % was 65.9, so this is a regression, not who Toronto is. Jakob Poeltl has played seven games and only 151 minutes, which may be part of it. If it persists, the defense depends entirely on forcing turnovers.

concerns.title: Defense slipping in November
concerns.body: After allowing 106.2 a game in October, Toronto has given up 121 in November, and the last five games ran 8.22 points a game worse than the season. Shooting guards in particular are torching it, taking 32.2% of the points against it versus a league share of 22.4%. The road trip explains some of this, but the guard defense is a real hole.

concerns.title: Health of the top of the roster
concerns.body: Leonard is Out after two games, and Barnes and Quickley are both Day-To-Day. Barnes carries a 31.9 USG %, but Toronto has been 13.2 points per 100 worse with him on the floor. That number is noisy in nine games, but it shows the team hasn't found its best structure yet.

trend.note: A strong October built on two blowouts gave way to a .500 November in which the defense leaked. The last five came in at 2-3 with a negative differential, most of it on the road.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, but Boston, Philly and New York test everything
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games are in Toronto, but the opponents are a strong set: Memphis is 8th on the site, Boston 2nd and New York 10th, and Philadelphia is 9-2. The week also lines up against Toronto's identity. New York leads the league in DRB % and Memphis is 3rd, so the offensive-rebounding edge will be contested in two of the four. Boston is the exception, sitting 25th in DRB %, so the glass should be open there.

The Philadelphia game is the clearest opening. The 76ers are 21st by ORtg, their W vs Pt Diff is the league's highest, and their Opp Rim Rate (29th) lets teams into the paint. Their 2nd-ranked TOV % blunts Toronto's ball pressure, though, and their A-graded backcourt goes straight at the shooting-guard weakness. A 2-2 week would be a fair result. Anything better means the shooting has started to turn.

keyMatchups.title: Glass war with New York, Memphis
keyMatchups.body: Toronto's top-ranked ORB % meets the league's best defensive rebounding team in New York and the 3rd-best in Memphis. If those teams finish possessions, Toronto loses its main source of extra shots and has to win on jump shooting, which hasn't been there.

keyMatchups.title: Boston's rim wall
keyMatchups.body: Boston ranks 3rd in Opp Rim FG % and 2nd in Opp Rim Rate, and its 119.6 ORtg is 2nd in the league. A team that shoots 31.5 from three can't easily punish a defense that walls off the paint. The Celtics' weak DRB % is Toronto's best path: putbacks rather than first shots.

keyMatchups.title: Turnover pressure vs Memphis
keyMatchups.body: Memphis is 18th in TOV %, the most turnover-prone offense on this week's slate. That makes the opener the best setup for Toronto's league-leading ball pressure. The Grizzlies' A-graded backcourt will also test a defense that gives up the most points to shooting guards.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Toronto can hold opposing guards down while Barnes and Quickley are listed Day-To-Day.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin pace (46 wins) and last season's 46-36 point to the same place: a team that should finish above .500. The parts of the profile pull in opposite directions. The 3P % is well below last season and should climb. The league-leading Opp TOV % is a jump of more than three points from last year and is the likeliest number to come back. An ORB % this far above anything in Toronto's recent history will probably settle too. Net, I expect ORtg to ease a bit and the record to track the margin.

The real swing is the rim defense. If Opp Rim FG % drifts back toward last season's 65.9, the defense can return to the top ten and Toronto lands in the low-to-mid 40s in wins. If it stays this porous once the turnovers dry up, this is a play-in team. Leonard's return is the upside case: he is the highest-ranked player on the roster by tab, and he has barely played.
swingFactors: Rim defense returning to last season's level
How much of the forced-turnover rate holds

confidence.note: Nine games, two blowouts and key players in and out; the style profile is clear, but the rates are early.
